summary: Harden the authenticated current-state snapshot by eliminating runtime third-party execution in the token realm, defining revocable authorization behavior and real-host verification, and making rejected permit navigation restore focus without an uncaught exception, while preserving all validated snapshot and analytical behavior.
assumptions: The three documented current-snapshot entity-search routes are existing authorized server contracts; no backend or SQL work is requested.
The host runtime exposes or can be adapted to the existing ready, executeCommand, and ToDisplayDate contracts without embedding credentials or inventing navigation parameters.
Equipment validity and overdue classification is intentionally unavailable until additional business rules are supplied; this does not block equipment total/facts or the other snapshot metrics.
Live authenticated verification may be unavailable locally and must not be represented as completed when skipped.

Approved SimplyLog parent and API origins are explicit configuration; production trust is HTTPS-only, while any localhost exception is isolated to test/development with synthetic credentials and data.
Performance timing ceilings are deterministic local regression budgets, not claims about live SimplyLog network latency.

An approved real SimplyLog test host or controller-owned faithful host harness is an external release-verification prerequisite; synthetic postMessage fixtures alone cannot close the authorization-lifecycle finding.

tasks.title: Secure executable loading and authenticated snapshot transport
tasks.component: Document dependency boundary, CSP, API client, and dataset constants
tasks.objective: Ensure only reviewed same-origin executable code runs in the bearer-token realm, then provide the three existing current-report searches with exact endpoint, authentication, empty-body, envelope, cancellation, and redaction behavior while leaving monthly analytical requests unchanged.
requirements: Replace the runtime jsDelivr XState script with the pinned xstate@4.38.3 browser artifact served from site/ or an equivalently reviewed local bundle; remove every runtime CDN import and remote executable fallback, and record the shipped artifact SHA-256.

Provide static-host response headers whose Content-Security-Policy includes default-src 'self', script-src 'self', object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', and only the minimum approved connect-src and embedding policy; do not allow unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, wildcard script sources, or meta-only enforcement.
Define currentEvents, currentPermits, and currentEquipment dataset keys for the exact documented POST routes.
Provide a current-search operation that sends JSON {} exactly once per dataset, using host ApiAddress, Authorization, Content-Type application/json, and AbortSignal.

Return both Items and normalized TotalCount for current reports; reject missing, non-array, negative, fractional, or nonnumeric TotalCount and incomplete/malformed envelopes, but leave dataset-specific cardinality checks to the adapters so equipment can deduplicate before population reconciliation.
Do not add dates, filters, location, pagination, username, or administrator identity to these requests, and do not change the existing analytical request body builder.

Before constructing any authorization-bearing URL, require an immutable host context created by the validated window.parent/approved-origin binding path and recognized by a non-forgeable module-private brand; a plain object with __trustedHostOrigin, or any other matching public shape, is unbound and rejected. If exposed for compatibility, __hostContextBound must also equal true but is not sufficient by itself.
Sanitize tokens and response errors; never log, persist, render, or place credentials in agent artifacts.
acceptanceCriteria: A snapshot load produces exactly three concurrent POSTs to the exact current-report paths and each serialized body equals {}.
The caller receives Items and TotalCount distinctly, so domain totals cannot be confused with envelope row counts.
Abort, HTTP/permission, network, invalid JSON, and malformed envelope failures remain typed errors and never resolve as empty arrays or zero metrics.
Existing monthly endpoint tests still observe their current date-range bodies without regression.
Rejected/unbound contexts and unapproved API origins cause zero snapshot or analytical authenticated requests.
The exact served document has an enforcing CSP response header, requests no third-party executable, and loads the pinned state-machine dependency from same-origin bytes matching the recorded digest.
validationScenarios: Capture fetch calls and assert method, URL, auth headers, body {}, and signal for all three current datasets.
Return 401, 403, missing procedure/server error, invalid JSON, missing Items, and invalid TotalCount; assert safe typed failures with no token leakage.
Run existing analytical API tests and confirm date bodies remain unchanged.

Inspect the exact preview response headers and browser request trace: assert CSP is present, script-src is self-only, the local dependency digest matches reviewed bytes, and no CDN or third-party script request occurs.

tasks.title: Map and validate current event, permit, and equipment reports
tasks.objective: Convert report envelopes into strict UI-ready snapshot data, reconcile scope counts, preserve permit semantics, deduplicate equipment facts, and explicitly withhold unsupported equipment validity classification.
requirements: Current events require exactly overall, headquarters, and branches rows with unique ScopeKey, non-negative integer TotalCount/OpenCount, OpenCount not exceeding TotalCount, and present AsOf.
Validate headquarters plus branches equals overall for both total and open counts; treat envelope TotalCount only as report row count.
Current permits require exactly one row with separate non-negative integer ValidCount, MissingCount, OverdueCount, plus AsOf and ValueDate; never derive or label a combined invalid count.

Equipment accepts the documented fact fields and nullable treatment/configuration fields, includes active and inactive items, and deduplicates by EquipmentId using a map; conflicting duplicates are invalid.

For equipment, validate envelope shape and TotalCount first, normalize and deduplicate rows second, then require TotalCount to equal the unique EquipmentId population. Do not require raw Items.length to equal TotalCount; identical duplicates are valid, while conflicting duplicates are invalid.
Map and deduplicate in one linear pass keyed by EquipmentId, retaining normalized output rather than obsolete raw response generations.
Report dates must remain raw adapter inputs for the host ToDisplayDate boundary; never append Z or parse them into analytical filters.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid fixtures map to event scope metrics, three separate permit metrics, and a deduplicated equipment total/facts collection; two identical rows for one EquipmentId with envelope TotalCount 1 succeed with total 1.
Any reconciliation, required-field, type, uniqueness, duplicate-conflict, or population mismatch yields invalid-response rather than fabricated data.
Inactive, never-treated, null-date, null-configuration, and arbitrary LastTreatmentStatus equipment stays countable but never receives a browser-invented valid/overdue result.
No displayed or mapped field calls Missing plus Overdue invalid certificates.

After one warm-up on the recorded project CI/runtime, a synthetic 10,000-row equipment envelope maps and deduplicates within 100 ms; duplicate-heavy input remains linear and returns the expected unique count.
validationScenarios: Map a reconciled three-row event response and reject missing scopes, duplicate scopes, open greater than total, and HQ/branches mismatches.
Map permit counts including zeros independently and reject multiple rows, negative/fractional counts, or missing report dates.

With Items containing two identical EquipmentId rows and TotalCount 1, assert successful deduplication to one fact; reject the same fixture when duplicate facts conflict or when TotalCount differs from the unique count. Also accept nullable treatment fields and inactive equipment.

Measure 0, 1, 1,000, and 10,000-row equipment fixtures, including duplicate-heavy and nullable variants, and record runtime/version, duration, unique count, retained normalized size, and decoded response bytes.
Assert equipment output exposes classification unavailable in all unresolved fact combinations.

tasks.title: Add an independent stale-safe snapshot lifecycle
tasks.component: Dashboard state machine and data orchestration
tasks.objective: Load the three current reports after authenticated host bootstrap with snapshot-local loading/error/ready/stale state, concurrency cancellation, and no coupling to analytical month selection.
requirements: Start snapshot loading only after one valid host context is accepted, in parallel with but logically independent from period discovery and monthly dashboard loading.
Track a snapshot request ID and AbortController; abort superseded loads and ignore every late completion whose ID is not current.
Fetch the three current reports concurrently and commit a coherent snapshot only after all validate.

For each initial load or refresh, issue exactly three requests, zero automatic retries, and at most three requests belonging to the current generation in flight; initiate the three calls within 50 ms under mocked transport.
Maintain snapshot-specific status, sanitized error, refreshedAt, and optional lastGoodData; first-load failure shows no numbers, refresh failure retains prior data marked stale.
Year/month selection must not clear, reload, or mutate snapshot state. An explicit/global refresh may start both lifecycles while preserving separate IDs and status.
Expose a snapshot retry that does not force analytical data to reload.
A 10-refresh burst aborts superseded work, commits only generation 10, retains at most one lastGoodData snapshot, and does not create a retry/request storm.

Key snapshot and analytical work to the accepted host-capability generation. On host invalidation/replacement or authenticated 401/403, revoke that generation, abort its in-flight requests, retain last-good values as stale, deny new authenticated work, and ignore all late completions until a fresh approved context is accepted.
acceptanceCriteria: The analytical dashboard can be ready while the snapshot is loading or failed, and the snapshot can be ready while analytical data changes period.
Changing year/month produces no current-report request and leaves snapshot data/timestamp intact.
Late success or failure from an aborted/superseded snapshot cannot overwrite the newest snapshot state.
A failed refresh retains last good snapshot values with stale/error treatment; an initial failure shows no zeros.
Period changes issue zero snapshot requests; one load/refresh issues exactly three with no pagination or automatic retry.

After authorization loss, no old-generation request can commit and no new authenticated request starts; fresh authorized re-entry creates a new generation and recovers without reusing the expired token.
validationScenarios: Drive host acceptance and assert snapshot and period loading begin without cross-clearing state.
Resolve two overlapping snapshot requests in reverse order and assert only the newest commits.
Change analytical periods during snapshot loading and assert independence and no extra current calls.
Test initial failure, retry success, and refresh failure with retained stale data.
Run a 10-refresh burst and assert only the newest generation commits, at most three newest-generation requests are active, and only one last-good snapshot is retained.

With a faithful host lifecycle fixture, revoke authorization during in-flight work, assert abort plus retained stale data and zero post-revocation authenticated calls, then supply fresh authorization and assert recovery from a new context generation.

tasks.title: Integrate host date formatting and permit-board navigation
tasks.component: Host service boundary and snapshot commands
tasks.objective: Use existing host services for report-date display and exact permit-board navigation while keeping permissions and navigation failures explicit.
requirements: Adapt the authenticated host integration to expose ready, executeCommand, and ToDisplayDate only from an immutable context produced by successful parent/source/origin validation. Brand bound contexts through module-private state or an equivalent non-forgeable factory boundary; a caller-supplied public marker is never sufficient.
Accept bootstrap and host-service messages only when event.source is window.parent and event.origin is an explicitly approved HTTPS parent origin; remove production-style HTTP trust.

Normalize ApiAddress to its origin and allow only approved HTTPS SimplyLog API origins corresponding to the trusted environment. Any localhost exception is explicit test/development-only and cannot carry a production bearer token.

Bind command and date-service responses to the same accepted parent source and origin. Direct/top-level access, timeout, malformed/rejected context, fallback mode, or response source/origin mismatch permits no authenticated fetch or privileged command.
Pass AsOf and ValueDate unchanged to ToDisplayDate; do not append Z or introduce local timezone interpretation.
All valid, missing, and overdue permit indicators call ready then executeCommand Navigate with exactly { Url: '#/Permits/Dashboard' } and no filter parameters.
Prevent duplicate activation while navigation is pending; restore interaction afterward and surface a non-destructive accessible failure if readiness or navigation rejects.

Capture the activating element before the first await; asynchronous cleanup must use that stable reference rather than event.currentTarget, and may restore focus only if the element remains connected and focusable.

Revoking or replacing the host capability while navigation is pending invalidates the command generation; reject any late response, clear the busy lock safely, retain snapshot data as stale, and issue no further privileged command until fresh approved bootstrap.
Twenty rapid activations while navigation is pending must produce exactly one ready/Navigate chain and unlock after either resolution or rejection.
Do not navigate from event or equipment metrics unless a separate contract is supplied.
acceptanceCriteria: Date display delegates each report value to the host adapter unchanged.
Each permit metric invokes the same exact unfiltered board URL after host readiness and no URL/query data is derived from the count.

Navigation failure leaves snapshot data visible, produces user-facing feedback without leaking internal response details, restores focus when the captured control is still eligible, and emits no uncaught exception when it is absent or rerendered.
Existing authenticated-host and permission behavior remains intact.

A same-origin non-parent sender, production HTTP origin, HTTP ApiAddress, unapproved HTTPS ApiAddress, direct access, mismatched command response, and an unbound plain object carrying an approved __trustedHostOrigin are rejected before any authenticated fetch or privileged command.
validationScenarios: Spy on ToDisplayDate and assert exact raw report date arguments without a Z suffix.
Activate each permit metric by click and keyboard and assert call order and exact Navigate payload.

Delay and reject host readiness/executeCommand; assert busy-lock, safe focus restoration, accessible error feedback, and zero pageerror or unhandledrejection events; repeat after removing or rerendering the activating control before settlement.

Exercise the negative trust-boundary matrix, including an approved-origin plain object with no valid binding brand and contexts mutated after creation, and assert zero authenticated requests/commands; then issue 20 rapid permit activations and assert one in-flight command chain.

tasks.title: Render the responsive accessible current snapshot
tasks.component: Dashboard snapshot region, metric cards, and styles
tasks.objective: Present event, permit, and equipment indicators as a Hebrew-first responsive region that follows runtime direction, preserves current charts, and clearly distinguishes unavailable data from zero.
requirements: Insert the current-snapshot region before analytical period controls/charts with a semantic heading, independent status, and refreshed/report-date context.
Show overall, headquarters, and branches event total/open values with labels that do not imply analytical-period filtering.
Show valid, missing, and overdue permits as three separately named native interactive controls; never present their sum as invalid.
Show total equipment and a textual valid/overdue classification unavailable state; do not render plausible placeholder numbers.
Provide snapshot-local loading, first-load error/retry, refresh-stale warning, and navigation-error presentation; use polite announcements without replacing the entire analytical dashboard.

After rejected permit navigation, keep sanitized accessible feedback visible and preserve focus on the captured permit control when it still exists; if rerender removed it, leave focus at a safe existing target without throwing.
Use logical layout properties, visible focus, sufficient contrast, locale-aware number formatting, and stacked small-screen layout. Preserve runtime RTL/LTR and existing chart/date-range behavior.
Render equipment only as aggregate total plus unavailable classification: input growth must add zero equipment fact/list nodes, and the entire ready snapshot must contain at most 80 DOM elements.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can distinguish current snapshot values from selected-month analytics, and changing the period does not visually clear the snapshot.
Zero is rendered only when supplied as a validated count; loading, errors, and unavailable classification use text/skeleton/status rather than 0.

All permit controls are keyboard reachable, have distinct accessible names, and retain visible focus; meaning is not conveyed by color alone, and rejected navigation never causes an uncaught focus-restoration error.
At narrow widths panels stack without horizontal clipping; at RTL and LTR directions reading order, spacing, and focus order remain coherent.
Existing analytical charts and controls remain present and functional.
On the recorded browser/runtime, one ready-state render completes within 50 ms at 390×844 and 1440×900 for the representative 10,000-row normalized fixture.
validationScenarios: Render ready data with real zeros and nonzeros; inspect accessible names and ensure unavailable equipment classification is textual.
Render loading, initial error, stale refresh error, and navigation failure without removing analytical content.
Check keyboard-only activation/focus and screen-reader status semantics.
Check phone/tablet/desktop widths in both dir=rtl and dir=ltr and verify existing chart regression.
Count snapshot DOM elements and measure one ready render at 390×844 and 1440×900; confirm the same node count for 1-row and 10,000-row equipment inputs.

tasks.title: Cover snapshot contracts, concurrency, UI, and regressions
tasks.component: Automated local test suite and fixtures
tasks.objective: Add deterministic tests proving exact current-report behavior, strict validation, concurrency safety, host integration, accessibility contracts, and preservation of existing analytics.
requirements: Use synthetic, non-secret fixtures for valid and malformed envelopes; do not copy raw controller/event payloads into tests.
Cover exact three-request transport behavior and ensure no pagination or date/filter fields are sent.

Cover mapper edge cases and event/equipment reconciliation, including nullable facts, inactive equipment, identical duplicate IDs accepted before envelope population reconciliation, conflicting duplicates rejected, unique-count mismatch rejected, and unavailable classification.
Cover independent state transitions, abort/stale suppression, retry, retained last-good data, and no fabricated zeros.
Cover exact host date/navigation calls, keyboard semantics, RTL/LTR markup/classes, and existing monthly dashboard regression.

Cover parent-window source binding, non-forgeable bound-context recognition, approved HTTPS parent/API origins, command-response and capability-generation binding, production HTTP rejection, unapproved API rejection, authorization revocation/re-entry, and zero authenticated fetch/command behavior for an unbound approved-origin-shaped object and in direct, timeout, fallback, malformed, mutated, expired, and rejected-context modes.

Cover the executable boundary: no remote script, import, or fallback; pinned local dependency digest; enforcing CSP response-header directives; and exact-preview network tracing that finds no third-party executable request.

Cover permit rejection cleanup in a browser by asserting sanitized feedback, unlocked controls, focus restored only to a still-connected captured element, and zero pageerror or unhandledrejection events when the element survives, is removed, or is rerendered.

Cover numeric performance budgets with 0/1/1,000/10,000-row and duplicate-heavy equipment fixtures, a 10-refresh burst, 20 rapid permit activations, fixed DOM count, render timings, request concurrency, and decoded-byte recording.
Keep tests local and deterministic; live credentials or provider availability must not be required.
acceptanceCriteria: All existing and new local tests pass with no secrets, network dependency, or live SimplyLog requirement.

Tests fail if a snapshot body gains a filter/date, if permit navigation gains parameters, if stale data overwrites current state, if equipment classification is inferred, if identical equipment duplicates are rejected before deduplication, or if an unbound host-shaped object is accepted.
Tests distinguish validated zero from loading/error/unavailable and protect existing analytical date/chart behavior.
Tests fail if a third-party executable is referenced or CSP permits it, if expired-context work commits or commands execute, or if rejected permit navigation throws during cleanup.

Recorded results identify CI/runtime and browser versions, fixture sizes, mapping/render durations, decoded bytes, DOM count, peak current-generation request count, and navigation command count; all stated numeric ceilings pass.
validationScenarios: Run the project test command and report pass/fail counts.
Inspect fixture and test output for credentials, raw event text, or signed URLs.
Run targeted API, mapper, machine, host, and UI contract tests plus the full regression suite.

Run and record the trust-boundary negative matrix, authorization revoke/re-entry fixture, dependency/CSP inspection, permit-rejection browser cases, and representative-volume performance suite, including actual measurements rather than pass/fail alone.

tasks.title: Document flag-safe verification and delivery evidence
tasks.component: Runtime flag boundary and verification record
tasks.objective: Make current-snapshot live-call enablement explicit and reversible for controller-owned verification, while honestly recording local and unavailable live checks without turning deployment into application implementation.
requirements: Keep CURRENT_SNAPSHOT_LIVE_CALLS_ENABLED false in default/local source state and isolate its effect to current snapshot calls, not monthly analytics.
Document that the controller may enable it for one authorized deployment without testsl verification; application work must not itself deploy or call lifecycle APIs.
Run all available local checks during implementation and record exact results; report authenticated live checks as skipped when host/runtime access is unavailable.

Record environment identity and performance evidence: runtime/CI version, browser/version, fixture row counts, decoded response bytes, mapping/render duration, DOM element count, request concurrency, refresh generation result, and navigation command count.
If verification cannot run, restore the local flag to false and do not request or trigger another deployment solely for the revert.
Do not claim procedure availability, production verification, or deployment completion from contract documentation alone.
For controller-run exact-preview evidence, record response headers, executable request URLs, local dependency digest, and confirmation that no third-party script executes in the token realm.

For release acceptance, use an approved real SimplyLog test host or controller-owned faithful host harness to prove authenticated bootstrap, authorization expiry or revocation, zero post-revocation authenticated requests and commands with retained stale data, fresh authorized re-entry, recovery, and command-response generation binding. Synthetic parent messaging alone must be labeled insufficient; if no approved environment is supplied, report this UAT as blocked or skipped and do not claim approval.
acceptanceCriteria: The delivered local source leaves the flag false unless the controller explicitly manages a temporary verification revision.
Verification evidence separates local automated checks from authenticated live checks and labels every skipped check honestly.
No Git, deployment, provider, SimplyLog lifecycle, SQL, or issue-tracker action is included in the implementation task.

Controller evidence closes the dependency finding only when the exact preview enforces CSP and makes no third-party executable request, and closes the lifecycle finding only when the approved real host or harness completes expiry and fresh re-entry without unauthorized requests or commands.
validationScenarios: Inspect the final local configuration and assert the live-call flag is false by default.
Review the verification record for exact commands/results and an explicit skipped-live-check reason when applicable.
Confirm no deployment artifact, SQL change, SearchAllEvents change, or lifecycle API call was introduced.

Run the exact preview through the approved host or harness, capture bootstrap to load to revoke or expire to stale and denied to fresh re-entry to recovery and navigation observations, and distinguish controller-run evidence from local synthetic checks.
